criteria.rationale: Read runtime_lanes.go and runtime_host.go:106-127: enter/admit/withdrawn/release keep queued and running balanced on every path; the -race integration check runs a heavy and a short command concurrently.
Reply.Metrics is an additive omitempty field; pose.runtime.status/1 and pose.runtime.run/1 are unchanged; runtimeSpawn signature change is internal.

parseRuntimeFlags (runtime_cmd.go:118-142) bounds each admission flag (slots/memo >=1, queues >=0, <=1048576) with a message naming the flag and range; a full lane refuses with a typed refused outcome.
start forwards the admission flags to the detached serve via serveArgs (runtime_cmd.go:105-108,195); the fixture spawn path in runtime_host_test.go exercises the same forwarding.
Examined Reply, Options and the status/run documents: only additive fields and new optional flags; defaults preserve prior behaviour apart from allowing concurrent lanes.

D1 basis R6: the cause (a 10 ms surface-check waiting behind a 25 s review-check under a single semaphore) is removed by a separate short lane; the classification follows the spec's measured timings (roadmap-check heavy).
Compared the change list with the spec's Artifacts: every implementation and doc file is listed; no CPU/cgroup limits or durable queue were added, matching the non-goals.
No new endpoint or authority; new inputs are bounded integers; metrics are non-sensitive counters; the env-digest and peer checks precede lane admission.

Minimal alternative (one-at-a-time) cannot meet R6; two static lanes with atomics and a channel are ~110 lines with no speculative extension. Invalidated if a short-listed command becomes slow or in-process concurrency races (see F4).

findings.action: runtimeReport never emits reply.Metrics in `pose runtime status --json` (pose.runtime.status/1) or in the human output, although R6 and POSE.md:947 say status carries the per-lane metrics; only the Go client API returns them, which is all the R6 test checks (runtime_host_test.go:317). The measurement consequently recorded runtime_metrics null.

The hosted-checks paragraph still states 'The runtime runs one hosted command at a time', contradicting the new lanes text in the same paragraph; same in locales/pt-BR/POSE.md:944 and both scaffold copies.
The 'Efetivo' line keeps '?' placeholders for admitted/refused counts and the JSON report has runtime_metrics null (line 81); R8 requires the report to state what was effective.
Update the comment and add a -race test running a real surface-check concurrently with a heavy check on a fixture project.
findings.rationale: Stale comment says hosted commands run one at a time because two would race; the in-process concurrency safety (D1 argues from separate processes) is only race-tested with `surface-check --help`, not real short-lane work beside a heavy check.

findings.action: Attribute memo hits per command (context-scoped counter) or document memo_hits as approximate under concurrency.
findings.rationale: memo_hits is the delta of a process-global counter; with concurrent lanes a command's reported memo_hits includes other commands' hits.

findings.action: Compare the short-query hosted outputs with a standalone surface-check output in the measurement.
findings.rationale: T5 claims every hosted output equals standalone, but surface-check outputs (idle and under heavy load) are never compared with a standalone run.

findings.action: Read VmHWM at the end of the resident scenarios, before the restart loop.
findings.rationale: T4 reads VmHWM before the short-query and concurrent heavy-load scenarios, so the reported peak excludes the concurrent phase.
